feed.title: Unadhi Guides
feed.subtitle: Free, sourced explainers for small businesses, CA firms, property buyers and exam candidates. Unadhi · One mind.

entry.title: E-way bill rules 2026: the ₹50,000 limit, validity by distance, Part B and extension
entry.summary: When an e-way bill is needed (consignment value above ₹50,000), how validity is counted (1 day per 200 km), when Part B can be skipped, extension and cancellation. Official GST sources.

entry.title: GST registration threshold 2026: ₹40 lakh, ₹20 lakh or ₹10 lakh, and who must register anyway
entry.summary: Which GST registration limit applies to you (goods vs services, your state), what counts in aggregate turnover, the cases where registration is compulsory at any turnover, and the 30-day deadline.

entry.title: INC-20A commencement of business: 180-day deadline, penalty and strike-off risk
entry.summary: Section 10A: a company with share capital must file INC-20A within 180 days of incorporation. Penalty ₹50,000 on the company, ₹1,000 a day on officers (max ₹1 lakh), and ROC strike-off risk.

entry.title: GST on an under-construction flat in Hyderabad: 5%, 1% affordable, and 0% after the OC
entry.summary: Buying a flat in Hyderabad? Under-construction homes attract 5% GST (1% if affordable: up to 60 sq m carpet in Hyderabad and up to ₹45 lakh). Ready flats with a completion certificate attract no GST.

entry.title: Paid promotion rules for Indian creators: how to disclose ads (Telugu creators' guide)
entry.summary: The Consumer Affairs 'Endorsement Know-hows' and CCPA misleading-ad guidelines in plain words for YouTube and Instagram creators: what counts as a paid tie-up, where the label goes, and the penalties.

entry.title: Explosives magazine licence for mines and quarries: PESO steps and common mistakes
entry.summary: Storing explosives for blasting needs a magazine licence from PESO under the Explosives Act 1884 and Explosives Rules 2008. The steps: site plan approval, district NOC, construction, inspection, licence and renewal.

entry.title: EU AI Act fines for SMEs: Article 99 tiers and the 'lower amount' rule
entry.summary: Article 99 sets three fine tiers (€35m/7%, €15m/3%, €7.5m/1%). For SMEs and start-ups the cap is whichever is lower. Worked examples and what reduces a fine.

entry.title: EU AI Act fundamental rights impact assessment (Article 27): who must do one and what goes in it
entry.summary: Article 27 FRIA: required for public bodies and private providers of public services using Annex III high-risk AI, and for credit scoring and life/health insurance pricing. The six required contents and how it links to a DPIA.

entry.title: EU AI Act authorised representative (Article 22): does a non-EU or Indian AI provider need one?
entry.summary: Article 22: providers outside the EU must appoint an EU authorised representative by written mandate before offering high-risk AI in the EU; Article 54 does the same for general-purpose AI models. Tasks, timing and who doesn't need one.

entry.title: EU VAT SME scheme since 2025: the €100,000 cross-border exemption and the EX number
entry.summary: Since 1 January 2025 (Directive (EU) 2020/285) small EU businesses can use the VAT exemption in other Member States if EU-wide turnover is €100,000 or less. Notification, the EX number, quarterly reporting and common errors.

entry.title: OPC registration on MCA V3: 8 mistakes that cause resubmission (2026)
entry.summary: Registering a One Person Company through SPICe+ on MCA V3? The 8 mistakes that send forms back or cause problems later: member and nominee eligibility, the 20-day name window, INC-22, MoA/AoA and more.

entry.title: One Person Company vs sole proprietorship in India: which fits you (2026)
entry.summary: OPC or proprietorship? A plain comparison for one-owner businesses in India: legal identity, liability, eligibility, paperwork every year, adding partners and when an OPC is worth it.

entry.title: '7000 ka penalty' on a nil GST return? GSTR-3B late fee caps explained (2026)
entry.summary: Paid a big late fee for months with zero business? Since June 2021 the GSTR-3B late fee per return is capped: ₹250 CGST for nil returns, ₹1,000 or ₹2,500 for others by turnover. Why it still adds up.

entry.title: EU AI Act AI literacy (Article 4): what a small business must actually provide
entry.summary: Article 4 of the EU AI Act has applied since 2 Feb 2025 to anyone who provides or uses AI systems. After the AI Omnibus: no certificate, no mandated level, no test. What to do, in 4 steps.

entry.title: 'Every time I think I understand OSS…': EU €10,000 threshold and OSS return, plainly

entry.summary: CBDT Circular 7/2026 moved the tax audit report for FY 2025-26 from 30 Sep to 21 Oct 2026, and the matching ITR to 21 Nov 2026. Who is covered and who is not.

entry.summary: Under QRMP, quarterly GSTR-3B is due on the 22nd (Telangana, AP, Karnataka, Maharashtra and others) or the 24th (Delhi, UP, West Bengal and others). Jul–Sep 2026: 22 or 24 Oct.

entry.summary: If you are a Udyam-registered micro or small supplier, buyers must pay within 45 days (15 if nothing agreed). Interest at 3x RBI bank rate, s.43B(h), and the MSME ODR portal.

entry.title: Form 124 (new 12BB) for HRA in 2026: landlord PAN, relationship, rent receipts
entry.summary: From tax year 2026-27, Form 124 replaces Form 12BB. For HRA: landlord name, address, PAN if rent is over ₹1 lakh a year, and your relationship with the landlord.

entry.title: TDS late filing fee 2026: ₹200 a day under section 427 (old 234E), and the 30 Nov 2026 penalty line
entry.summary: Under the Income-tax Act 2025, a late TDS/TCS statement costs ₹200 a day (s.427, was 234E), capped at the TDS. File within one month of the due date to avoid the s.461 penalty. Examples.

entry.title: GST interest calculation 2026: 18% a year on the cash part, with examples (section 50, Rule 88B)
entry.summary: Late GSTR-3B? Interest is 18% a year under section 50(1), on the tax paid in cash, for the days of delay (Rule 88B). Wrong ITC used: 18% under 50(3). Formula, examples and mistakes.

entry.title: Diwali bonus and gifts: tax rules for 2026-27 (₹15,000 employer gift limit, ₹50,000 rule)
entry.summary: A cash Diwali bonus is salary. Employer gifts and vouchers are tax-free only below ₹15,000 a year in total (new 2026 Rules). Gifts from friends: taxable above ₹50,000. Relatives: exempt.

entry.title: Udyam (MSME) registration 2026: free, step by step, and the micro/small limits in force since April 2025
entry.summary: Udyam registration is free, paperless and needs only Aadhaar plus PAN/GSTIN. Steps on udyamregistration.gov.in, the 2025 micro/small/medium limits, Udyam Assist, and mistakes to avoid.

entry.title: GST for Indian freelancers with foreign clients (2026): the ₹20 lakh threshold, export of services and LUT
entry.summary: Export of services counts toward the ₹20 lakh GST threshold (₹10 lakh in four NE states). Below it you can stay unregistered; above it, register and file a LUT to bill abroad without IGST.
